name: Social Mirror and Embodied Social Presence
short_description: Observing others' actions activates mirror system (premotor, IPL) for motor simulation and anterior insula for empathic affect; modulates approach tendency; creates 'social atmosphere' phenomenology
higher_order_principle: Observing others' actions and emotional states in a shared space activates mirror system (premotor, IPL) for motor simulation and anterior insula for empathic affect. This embodied resonance modulates approach tendency and creates the phenomenological sense of 'social atmosphere.' Strength scales with proximity, visual angle, and number of visible others.
scope_conditions: Requires visual access to other people (not merely knowing they are present)
Mirror activation is automatic — cannot be voluntarily suppressed when others are visible
Modulated by social identity: in-group members produce stronger resonance than out-group
Affective contagion can be negative: hospital waiting areas, distressed crowds produce vicarious distress
moderators: number_of_visible_others (more people → stronger ambient resonance, up to saturation ~25-30)
emotional_valence_of_crowd (positive crowd → positive contagion; negative → negative)
glass_and_transparency (glass walls provide visual access without acoustic coupling — 'aquarium effect')

interactions.nature: T48 = top-down mentalizing, T49 = bottom-up embodied simulation. Both operate simultaneously but on different timescales (T49 faster, ~100ms; T48 slower, ~300ms).
Empathic resonance in anterior insula uses same substrate as interoceptive processing. Social empathy IS a form of interoception — simulating another's body state.
